decisions.reason: The existing message-434 MODIFY already records the 3.4V programmed DCDC1 output and its Schottky-drop compensation purpose; no additional update or removal is required.
The existing message-434 MODIFY already records that the power-board input carries the 3.4V DCDC1 output and that the main-board Schottky drop produces the 3.3V system rail.
The DCDC1 compensation change does not alter USB data routing, enumeration, flashing, or standalone programming; the system rail remains 3.3V.
Current monitoring remains downstream of the Schottky diodes on the regulated 3.3V system rail, so its device, position, rails, and measurement coverage remain unchanged.
AXP2101 remains the normal-operation power source and the battery path and load coverage are unchanged; only DCDC1's programmed pre-diode voltage changes.
The DCDC1 output adjustment does not change the selected USB-C connector, its data support, sourceability, or substitute requirements.
The panel-button behavior is independently introduced by the first clause of message 434 and is not changed by the source Event's DCDC1 voltage decision.
The charge-status interface still receives a 3.3V system rail after the Schottky drop; its LED method, connector, resistor, and population requirements are unchanged.
The source decision concerns DCDC1 compensation for the 3.3V rail and does not change the 5V boost converter, enable control, routing, rating, or powered loads.
The compensated post-diode rail remains 3.3V, so the I2C pull-up voltage, resistance, placement, and series-resistor policy remain valid unchanged.
The sensor board continues to receive a 3V3 rail from the main board; the pre-diode DCDC1 adjustment does not change its connector fanout or signal assignments.
The DCDC1 adjustment keeps the post-diode system rail at 3.3V and does not change the LED daughterboard's selected part, package, count, or recorded supply requirement.
